queries.hook: A resolve forged in fourteen months of nothing and now proven real; the readiness to keep going when the highs fade and the lows come.
queries.diagnose: Resolve fades when the mind runs ahead to the prize or looks sideways at others; it holds when the work itself is the reward.
queries.steady: No honest effort on the right path is ever wasted; even a little of it protects you and carries you forward.
queries.act: Rise and act; do your work fully and well each day, let the result go, and keep at it when no one is watching.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
verse.sanskrit: मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहंवादी धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः । सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योर्निर्विकारः कर्ता सात्त्विक उच्यते ॥
verse.line: Free of clinging and boasting, full of resolve and enthusiasm, unchanged by success or failure: the best kind of doer.
verse.translation: The doer who is free from attachment, does not speak of himself, is full of steadiness and enthusiasm, and unmoved by success or failure, is called sattvic.
verse.why: Choose the joy that's hard at first and sweet later.

prasang.title: Knowledge, action, doer, intellect, resolve and happiness by the three gunas
prasang.summary: Krishna describes clear, restless and dull versions of action, doer, judgement, resolve and happiness: the best joy is poison first and nectar later; the restless kind is nectar first and poison later.
prasang.lesson: Choose the joy that's hard at first and sweet later.

verse.meaning: Krishna is sorting the qualities of action and happiness. He describes a person who acts without clinging to the results, who does not boast, and who keeps a steady enthusiasm. This person does not swing up or down with success or failure. That is the highest kind of action.
verse.for_you: You signed the customer yesterday. The numbers are real, but the feeling that it might all be nothing is already waiting. This verse says the best way to move is to choose the joy that is hard at first and sweet later, not the other way around.

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha teaches the disheartened young Rama that effort, not fate, shapes his life.
verse.sanskrit: पुरुषार्थात्फलप्राप्तिर्देशकालवशादिह । प्राप्ता चिरेण शीघ्रं वा यासौ दैवमिति स्मृता ॥
verse.line: Effort brings results, sooner or later, depending on time and place. That timing is what we call fate.
verse.translation: Results come from effort, sooner or later, depending on place and time. That arrival of the fruit, early or late, is what people call fate.
verse.why: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

prasang.title: Vasishtha on self-effort: fate is only your past effort
prasang.summary: Vasishtha's first teaching to Rama is a long case for self-effort. What people call fate is simply the fruit of their own past effort, and present effort can overcome it, as the stronger of two rams wins. He also says not to torment yourself over what was beyond your power, and to steer your habits gently, like raising a child.
prasang.lesson: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

verse.meaning: Vasishtha speaks to the young Rama, who has just lost his father and his kingdom, teaching him that the world does not run on luck. He says that effort brings results, sooner or later, depending on time and place. That arrival of the fruit, early or late, is what people call fate.
verse.for_you: The first payment is the result of the fourteen months you already put in. The next one is already in your hands, waiting for the next effort. Let the numbers move or pause. Your part is to keep the work steady.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: निन्दन्तु नीतिनिपुणा यदि वा स्तुवन्तु लक्ष्मीः समाविशतु गच्छतु वा यथेष्टम् । अद्यैव वा मरणमस्तु युगान्तरे वा न्याय्यात्पथः प्रविचलन्ति पदं न धीराः ॥
verse.line: Let them praise or blame, let money come or go: the steady don't step off the right path.
verse.translation: Let the worldly-wise blame or praise; let fortune come or go as she pleases; let death come today or ages hence: the steadfast do not move a step from the path of what is right.
verse.why: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
prasang.summary: Steadfastness: the gods kept churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar; the steady do not leave the right path whatever people say. A struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.
prasang.lesson: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari speaks to the reader from the section on steadfastness. The verse says let the worldly-wise blame or praise. Let fortune come or go as she pleases. Let death come today or ages hence: the steadfast do not move a step from the path of what is right. This means that setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path. The idea carries forward into your life.
verse.for_you: You signed your first paying customer yesterday. The praise is still ringing, but you know the next twelve months are about not moving a step from the path. When the numbers stop moving, let that be the moment you hold the line.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Arjuna asks what becomes of someone who tries and fails; Krishna reassures him.
verse.sanskrit: पूर्वाभ्यासेन तेनैव ह्रियते ह्यवशोऽपि सः । जिज्ञासुरपि योगस्य शब्दब्रह्मातिवर्तते ॥
verse.line: Past practice carries you forward, even when you don't feel like it.
verse.translation: By that former practice he is carried on, even against his will. Even one who merely wishes to know yoga goes beyond the ritual word.
verse.why: No sincere effort is wasted; you pick up where you left off.

prasang.title: What becomes of one who falls from yoga
prasang.summary: Arjuna fears that one who falls short is lost like a torn cloud. Krishna promises that no one who does good comes to ruin; past effort carries forward and they strive again.
prasang.lesson: No sincere effort is wasted; you pick up where you left off.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna at a moment when Arjuna fears that a failed attempt at yoga is ruined and gone. Krishna answers that no sincere effort is wasted. A person is carried forward by the practice they already have, even when they do not feel like it. The wish to know the path is enough to carry them beyond mere ritual. What came before is not lost. It is what picks them up and moves them on.
verse.for_you: You have already spent fourteen months building. That practice is still working even now, in the quiet before the next big number. It is what will carry you forward when the early excitement fades.

verse.speaker: Janaka's doorkeeper
verse.setting: As Janaka sits lost in thought, his doorkeeper reminds him the day's work is waiting.
verse.sanskrit: शीघ्रमुत्तिष्ठ भद्रं ते नियतं कार्यमाचर । न कालमतिवर्तन्ते महान्तः स्वेषु कर्मसु ॥
verse.line: Get up and do today's work. Great people don't let the hour slip by.
verse.translation: Rise quickly, bless you, and do your appointed work. The great do not let the time slip by in their own duties.
verse.why: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

prasang.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
prasang.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
prasang.story_hook: One spring morning, a king out for a walk overheard a song that he could not stop thinking about.
prasang.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

verse.meaning: Janaka, the king, is sitting on his palace roof, shaken by what he has heard. His doorkeeper comes to call him down. The doorkeeper says the day's work is waiting. Janaka gets up and does his duties. The verse says that great people do not let the hour slip by in their own duties. You do not have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that does not clutch.
verse.for_you: You have a customer. The roof is a good place to sit, but the hour is slipping. Get up and do one small thing for the business today, and let your mind stay open to what comes next.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
verse.line: Your work is yours to do; the results are not yours to hold. Don't let that make you stop.
verse.translation: Your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruit be your motive, and do not cling to doing nothing.
verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.
verse.misuse: This is not 'don't care about results' or 'don't plan'. Care, plan and aim well; just don't let the outcome own you.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna on the battlefield, at a moment when Arjuna wants to drop his weapons and walk away. Krishna tells him to stand his ground and do his duty. Your work is yours to do. The results are not yours to hold. Don't let that make you stop.
verse.for_you: Sign the contract with the first paying customer. Let the money arrive, but do not let it decide if you stay. The work is yours. Do it fully, then step back and let the result live on its own.

story.title: Hanuman's leap
story.story_hook: Halfway across the ocean, a golden mountain rose out of the water and offered him a place to rest.
story.summary: Hanuman leaps across the ocean. A mountain rises to repay an old kindness by offering rest; he thanks it but keeps his promise not to stop. He outwits Surasa by shrinking small and defeats Simhika, and the watching beings praise his steadiness, sight, judgement and skill.
story.lesson: Gratitude and focus can go together; know when to be big and when to be small.

anchor.speaker: Beings of the sky
anchor.setting: Having outwitted two monsters mid-flight, Hanuman is praised by those watching from the sky.
anchor.sanskrit: यस्य त्वेतानि चत्वारि वानरेन्द्र यथा तव। धृतिर्दृष्टिर्मतिर्दाक्ष्य स कर्मसु न सीदति ॥
anchor.line: Steadiness, clear sight, good judgement and skill. With these four, you won't sink at work.
anchor.translation: Whoever has these four, as you do, chief of monkeys, never sinks in his work: steadiness, clear sight, judgement and skill.
anchor.why: Gratitude and focus can go together; know when to be big and when to be small.

story.for_you: You stand in that same place, with the first stone laid but the dry season ahead. The mountain of Mainaka is the comfort of your early wins. The vow is the fourteen months of work that brought you here. Let the mountain offer its rest, but do not let it become your home.

script: You signed the customer yesterday. The numbers are real, but the feeling that it might all be nothing is already waiting.
Arjuna is on the battlefield, confused and afraid, and Krishna is sorting the qualities of action and happiness for him. And Krishna replied:
मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहंवादी धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः, सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योर्निर्विकारः कर्ता सात्त्विक उच्यते.
In plain words: Free of clinging and boasting, full of resolve and enthusiasm, unchanged by success or failure: the best kind of doer.

This is the best kind of doer. They act without clinging to the results, without boasting, and with steady enthusiasm. They do not swing up or down with success or failure. This is easier said than done, because the more you care about the result, the more you will ride the highs and lows. The joy that is hard at first and sweet later is the only joy that will not leave you.
When the numbers stop moving, let the work itself be the thing you care about. Let the next small task be enough. Do not look ahead to see if it is working. Just do the next thing.
What is the one small thing you can do tomorrow that is just for the work itself?

depth.life: You have just signed your first paying customer, and the numbers are finally real. But the relief is thin. You know the real work starts now, and the old fear is already waiting, the one that says this was all for nothing.
depth.practice: Notice one moment today when you feel the urge to boast about the new customer, and instead let the feeling pass without speaking of it.
depth.question: When the numbers stop moving, what will you hold onto?
